description: We are a team of school students interested in coding and space science
summary: Our project, Beyond the Quantum Sky, is an interactive website in response to the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: NASA’s Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.” It looks at machines and instruments left behind during space missions and explains their work, discoveries and whether they are still working. The website has Apollo lunar equipment such as laser reflectors and science stations, Mars rovers like Opportunity, Curiosity and Perseverance and the Voyager spacecraft. It's also a guide to space hardware, including power systems, communication, computers, scientific instruments, and the challenges of surviving extreme conditions. Visitors can visit a variety of destinations, test their knowledge with a Mission Control quiz and find official NASA resources. This is a challenge that the project seeks to solve by making it easier to discover and understand the stories and contributions of these machines. It’s important because it keeps their legacy alive, demonstrates how missions to space continue to benefit science long after they’re done, and inspires students and future explorers.
details: Space-Time Capsules is an interactive educational website about NASA’s forgotten hardware on the Moon and Mars, their missions, discoveries, and contributions to science. It includes information about space missions, a guide to space hardware, interactive segments on destinations, a Mission Control quiz and links to official NASA resources. We have created it in HTML and CSS and given it a nice space themed design. The project makes learning about space more interesting, and preserves the legacy of past missions. We focused on accuracy, creativity, simplicity and easy navigation. Our aim is to raise awareness about space exploration, show how forgotten equipment is still contributing to science and encourage students and future explorers to learn more about space and technology.
